messages:
Marin Chen: FYI — ACME escalated. They say audit export missing HSM key usage lines AND their billing shows a large spike yesterday. Asking for scope, timeline, and concrete repro steps.
Sara K: Got the customer repro they sent. Short: API calls to /v1/generate returning 500 intermittently, then billing shows retries counted as tokens.
Alex R: Oncall triage: can we confirm if retries are deduped on our side?
Cal Patel: Security note: HSM/KMS logs are separate — if export omitted key-usage entries that’s likely post-processing or export filter. Not the HSM itself.
Priya Gomez: Customer wants an official timeline for when logs were available and when we exported. They asked for wording for customer-facing notif.
Alex R: I can reproduce 500s locally when autoscaler bounces a pod and the request hits a worker during KVcache warmup. Repro steps: 
```bash
# reproduce from their request pattern
for i in {1..50}; do curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"prompt":"test","max_tokens":64}' || echo "fail:$i"; done
```
Responses: mix of 200 and fast 500s with stack trace pointing at inference-engine timeout.
Sara K: Customer also included error snippet: 
```
ERROR 2026-05-03T14:12:09Z inference: request=abcd123 timeout after 250ms -> code=500
KMS: key-access denied? (403) for key=projects/..../keys/acme-key
```
Cal Patel: If there's a 403 from KMS, that indicates a separate auth event. Need KMS audit entries (Cloud HSM) for that timestamp window. If export omitted those lines, we need to confirm export filters.
incident-bot: export job finished: audit-export-2026-05-03T14:00-15:00 tarball created (sha256:fa3b...).
Alex R: I pulled the tarball — syslog has inference timeouts, but KMS access lines are present in the raw HSM logs. The CSV export we ship to customers had a filter that drops internal KMS debug lines.
Marin Chen: So plausible cause: customer-facing audit CSV omitted KMS debug rows -> they think HSM didn't log access. But actual HSM/audit has entries. Need to confirm billing spike cause separately.
Priya Gomez: For customer note: propose we say "we verified HSM audit logs show key access for your tenant during the requested window; a post-processing filter removed debug-level rows from the CSV export which we will correct." Thoughts? :thumbsup:
Legal Team: We need to be careful on phrasing re: "we verified" — legal wants timestamps and evidence attached to the notification. Also check if any exported files were delivered to third parties.
Alex R: I can attach the raw HSM log snippets and the exact CSV filter rule. Example raw lines I will redact tenant IDs in: 
```
2026-05-03T14:12:09Z HSM key=acme-key action=Encrypt user=svc-inference request_id=abcd123
2026-05-03T14:12:09Z KMS auth=GRANTED subject=service-account@redwood.iam
```
Sara K: Billing team: any idea why token counts jump? Customer reported ~3x tokens during the event.
Cal Patel: If retries are counted as separate generation calls, that would inflate token counts. We need to confirm whether client retried or our internal retry layer did.
incident-bot: billing-alert: spike detected for tenant acme (2026-05-03T14:00-15:00) usage +280% compared to baseline.
Alex R: I checked request logs: many requests returned 500 then immediately retried by client within 200ms. Our gateway logs show repeated requests with same client request-id but different internal ids — retries were treated as new billable calls.
Priya Gomez: Customer asked for timeline & mitigation. Proposed timeline draft: 1) 14:00–14:15 sporadic inference timeouts due to autoscaler warmup; 2) 14:12 observed KMS auth attempts — present in raw logs; 3) 14:12–14:20 client retries led to inflated token counts; 4) 14:30 export job produced CSV with debug rows filtered out.
Marin Chen: Next actions: Alex prepare attachments (redacted raw HSM lines + CSV filter config). Cal to confirm no keys compromised. Billing to propose credit for inflated tokens. Legal to review customer notification language. Priya to coordinate customer message and expected timeline.
Cal Patel: Quick check — keys show normal access patterns, no anomalies besides the expected service-account access. No evidence of exfil.
Sara K: I'll file a support ticket for the customer notif draft and include repro steps and logs.
Alex R: ETA for attachments: 1.5h.
Priya Gomez: I'll schedule a call with ACME for 17:00 today and share our draft.
Marin Chen: Thanks team. Keep replies short in this thread so I can copy-paste into the incident doc. :white_check_mark:
